messages:
opsbot: ALERT: spike in 429s for multiple orgs starting at 1791002468 — rate-limiter returned PER_KEY_BURST_EXCEEDED for many tokens

samir (eng-platform): seeing it too, ~15% of requests to /v1/generate are 429 across prod regions :grimacing:

mia (eng-sre): initial eyeball: latency normal, error is immediate 429, looks like quota/burst enforcement, not upstream timeout

kevin (eng-runtime): recent rollout to rate-limiter had change to apply per-org fallback when burst window missing. Could be related. I rolled a small config change yesterday night.

samir (eng-platform): timeline: config change merged 1790920000, config-watcher deployed 1790960000. We saw normal until ~1791002468 when errors spiked.

mia (eng-sre): quick check: consul shows policy for some orgs with "burst_window_ms": 0 and "burst_tokens": 0 — that would immediately throttle fanout tokens.

kevin (eng-runtime): whoa. That 0 wasn't intended. Our staging test sets 0 for a flag but should never be applied to prod orgs. Could be stale cached artifact.

samir (eng-platform): looking at config-watcher logs: it reads config generation 42, then fails to fetch new generation due to transient 504 from config-store. It retried and kept the last cached entry for many org entries. The cached entry looks like an older default that had zero burst values for uninitialized orgs.

mia (eng-sre): confirmed: tokens in fanout path used per-key enforcement which uses cached per-org policy. Cached default = zero-burst -> immediate 429. So thousands of tokens got blanket throttle. Root cause: stale cache + an unsafe default.

kevin (eng-runtime): mitigation options: a) hotpatch config-watcher to treat missing fields as unlimited-burst for a short window, b) clear config-cache across hosts, c) roll back the watcher to prior behavior. What’s fastest?

samir (eng-platform): fastest is clearing caches and forcing a new generation read. I'll run the cache-clear command on rate-limiter fleet and bump generation.

samir (eng-platform): running: 
```
# clear local caches via admin endpoint
for host in $(cat rate_limiter_hosts.txt); do 
  curl -s -XPOST http://$host:8080/admin/clear-config-cache || echo "fail $host"
done
# then bump config generation
curl -s -XPOST https://config-store.internal/api/v1/generations/claim -d '{"generation":43}'
```

deploy-bot: deployment started: config-watcher v2.1.3 -> v2.1.4 (hotfix) by samir

mia (eng-sre): performing canary: region-us-east now at ~0.5% 429s -> down to baseline after clear, continuing rollout

nina (product): any customer-facing impact? We had a support ticket about degraded UX — looks like that was this.

samir (eng-platform): customer impact: intermittent 429s for some high-fanout orgs for ~12m. We will notify affected customers.

kevin (eng-runtime): postmortem next steps: 1) change safe default to allow short burst instead of zero; 2) add config-mismatch alert when cached_generation != latest_generation on >1% hosts for >30s; 3) make config-watcher fall back to previous policy rather than cached default when fetch fails; 4) add unit test simulating config-store fail to ensure we don't apply empty/zero defaults.

mia (eng-sre): opened incident ticket IR-2026-1791 with action items. I'll own follow-ups on alerts and runbook updates.

samir (eng-platform): thanks. I'll prepare a short customer note and a changelog entry for the config default fix.

kevin (eng-runtime): adding a small dump from one rate-limiter host that showed the bad cached policy:
```
{"org":"org_123","policy":{"per_key_rate":20,"burst_tokens":0,"burst_window_ms":0,"generation":42}}
```

mia (eng-sre): eventual mitigation confirmed — 429s returned to baseline by 1791003120 after cache clear + watcher hotfix rollout. Closing active incident. Follow-ups tracked in IR-2026-1791. :white_check_mark:

opsbot: INCIDENT CLOSED by mia (eng-sre) at 1791003120
